answer: No garden may open its sluice out of turn. The roster keeper chalks each family's watering hour on the garden wall at dawn, and a gate opened early steals a neighbour's water. A nectar hour claimed without a chalk mark fails the wall: at the crystal of the roster the family's name must stand beside the hour it claims, and an unchalked gate is shut by the keeper on the spot. Cheating the roster takes bribing the keeper, altering 160 dawn chalks, paying 6,900, while the anchor chalk on the wall is checked by every gardener before the sluice is touched, so water drawn out of turn is cut off.
